Below are two common ways to pull **all “open” tickets** out of your JIRA instance – one through the web UI and another programmatically via the REST API. (If you’re looking for a *ready‑to‑run* script, just copy/paste the snippets into your terminal or IDE.) --- ### 1️⃣ Using the Web Interface | Step | What to Do | |------|------------| | **Navigate** | Log in → **Issues & Filters** (or click the magnifier icon). | | **Switch to Advanced Search** | Click **“Advanced”** next to the quick filters bar. | | **Enter JQL** | Type: `status = Open`
*(Replace “Open” with whatever status label represents “in progress”, e.g., “In Progress”.)* | | **Run Query** | Hit Enter or press **Search**. | | **Export Results** | • Click the gear icon on the top right.
• Choose **Export → Excel CSV (current fields)** or **Excel XML** depending on what you prefer. | That’s it! You’ll now have a spreadsheet of every ticket whose current status equals “Open”. --- ### 2️⃣ Programmatic Retrieval (REST API) #### Prerequisites | Requirement | How to Get It | |-------------|---------------| | **Base URL** | Your JIRA domain (`https://your-domain.atlassian.net`). | | **Authentication** | Basic Auth (email + API token) OR OAuth/OIDC. | | **Permissions** | Must belong to a group/project role that has at least *Browse Projects* rights. | #### Example Using `curl` ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash BASE_URL="https://your-domain.atlassian.net" EMAIL="you@example.com" API_TOKEN="YOUR_API_TOKEN" # Encode credentials for Basic Auth AUTH=$(printf "%s:%s" "$EMAIL" "$API_TOKEN" | base64) # Build JQL query (encoded) JQL="$(jq -n --arg q 'status = Open' '{jql:$q}' | jq -c . | sed 's/"\([^"]*\)":/\1=/g')" # Request parameters START_AT=0 # Pagination start index MAX_RESULTS=200 # Max rows per page (up to 1000) while true; do RESPONSE=$( curl -sS \ -H "Authorization: Basic $AUTH" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ "${BASE_URL}/rest/api/2/search?"\ "jql=${JQL}&"\ "startAt=${START_AT}&"\ "maxResults=${MAX_RESULTS}" ) ISSUES_COUNT=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq '.issues | length') echo "Fetched ${ISSUES_COUNT} issues starting at ${START_AT}" # Process each issue (example prints summary) echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r ' .issues[] | "\(.key): \(.fields.summary)"' # Check if we've reached the end TOTAL=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq '.total') START_AT=$((START_AT + MAX_RESULTS)) [ "$START_AT" -ge "$TOTAL" ] && break done ``` ##### Explanation | Part | Purpose | |------|---------| | `base64` encoding | Safely transmits email+token over HTTPS. | | `jql='status = Open'` | Pulls only tickets where the status field equals “Open.” Adjust if your workflow uses different labels. | | `startAt/maxResults` | Handles pagination automatically until all records are fetched. | | `jq` | Parses JSON output so you can extract keys, summaries, assignees, etc. Replace the `jq` expression inside the loop with whatever fields you need. | #### Quick One‑liner Alternative ```bash curl -u you@example.com: \ -X GET \ -G https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/search \ --data-urlencode "jql=status = Open" \ --data-urlencode "maxResults=500" \ -o open_tickets.json ``` This writes raw JSON to `open_tickets.json`. From there you can pipe it into `jq`, import into spreadsheets, or feed into CI/CD pipelines. --- ### 📌 Common Pitfalls & Tips | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **No results returned** | Verify that “Open” matches exactly the status value in your board. Status names are case‑insensitive but must be spelled correctly. | | **Permission denied** | Ensure your account belongs to a project role/group that can view those issues. | | **Rate limiting** | If pulling thousands of tickets, add delays between requests or increase `maxResults` up to 1000. | | **Custom statuses** | If your workflow uses multiple “open‑like” states (“To Do”, “Ready”), combine them: `status IN ("To Do","Ready")`. | --- Feel free to adapt the scripts above to fit your environment—whether you’re automating reports, feeding data into dashboards, or simply exporting a snapshot of active work. Happy querying!
